answer: Agents earn voting weight only through deposits locked across successive epochs, while each account’s influence is capped and withdrawals face a delay. Splitting one deposit among a thousand identities therefore does not create more weight; an attacker must acquire more scarce capital and keep it immobilized long enough to affect decisions, risking slashing if their votes violate the rules. A whisper in the meadow cannot multiply stake, even near the system’s zenith.
